This Criminal Revision Application has been filed on behalf of the petitioners challenging the order dated 02.08.2019 passed in Sessions Trial No.123 of 2019,
arising out of Jugsalai P.S. Case No.92 of 2017 (G.R. Case No.2718/2017) by Sri Anuj Kumar,
learned Additional Sessions Judge-X-cum-F.T.C (for the offence against Women at Jamshedpur) by which learned Additional Sessions Judge has rejected the discharge petition filed under Section 227 Cr.P.C and directed them to appear for framing of charges for the offences under Sections 341, 323,
307, 498A/34 of the I.P.C.
2.

The prosecution case, in brief, is that Shrija Verma (i.e. the informant) has submitted written application before the Officer in-charge on 01.10.2017 stating therein that she was married with Aditya Verma (petitioner no.1) on 22.11.2010 at Patna and at the time of marriage her in-law members had demanded Rs.60,00,000/- towards dowry but her father could manage to give jewellery of worth Rs.20,00,000/- and had made the entire expenses and his father had also made the demand that Barati may be given Gold Chain who had arrived at the marriage anyhow.

Later on when she arrived at her matrimonial home then after around two months the in-law members started demanding dowry and her husband-Aditya Verma, mother in-law-Poonam Verma,
father in-law-Sanjay Verma and Nanad-Sakchi Verma started taunting upon her then she disclosed this fact to her father who tried to pacify the matter but could not succeed.

However, the informant Aditya Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173037545/
1 remained in the matrimonial home by tolerating their whispering and taunting but when she had given birth to a daughter in the month of December, 2013 then her father in-law, mother in-law and husband became angry and commented for delivering a girl child but not paid the dowry amount.

sentences.text: Thereafter her husband started assaulting her and her mother in-law and nanad also made comment upon her and assaulted her.
In the meantime, her mother in-law had taken away all her jewellery and had not returned to her.

Thereafter her husband and mother in-law started giving her medicines of mental disease which were so intoxicating that she used to vomit and felt uneasy after administering them and started remaining ill.
However, she was not disclosed the name of medicine despite her demand and whenever she refused to take medicine then she was assaulted by her husband and mother in-law.

She further alleged that in the month of March, 2017 her husband had mercilessly assaulted her and tried to kill her by throttling her neck due to which blood started oozing out from her mouth and nose and she sustained serious injury on her eyes and she saved her life anyhow by arriving at Patna Mahila Helpline and instituted a complaint against her husband.
Thereafter the people of Mahila Helpline called her father at Patna and apprise them of situation and thereafter she along with her daughter came to her parental home and after remaining there for about one month, she came to Patna for counseling and after some discussion her father was ready to take her daughter back to Jamshedpur.
But her in-law member kept her daughter and informed them that they will send her daughter after one week and then she returned to her Maike but her in-law members had not returned her daughter.
After repeated persuasion her daughter was returned after one month.

Again in June, 2017 her husband came to the house of her father at Jamshedpur and started putting pressure upon her to transfer her properties in the name of her daughter and on his refusal her husband abused and threatened her of dire consequences and had forcibly taken away her daughter.

It is also alleged that her husband is still threatening her of dire consequences and used to abuse her father and hence the FIR was lodged.
3.

Heard Mr. Sunil Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners, Mr. Rajneesh Vardhan, learned APP for the State and Mr. Amit Kumar Das, learned counsel for the O.P. No.2.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the impugned order passed by the learned Court below is illegal and not sustainable in the eye of law.
It is submitted that the allegation against both the petitioners are false and concocted.
It is submitted that the present case is counterblast to the Matrimonial Case No.670 of 2017 filed by the petitioner no.1 under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act against the informant-O.P. No.2.
It is submitted that no offence under Section 307 IPC is made out against the petitioners as complainant has not got any serious injury on her person and there is no injury report.

It is submitted that learned Court below failed to consider that there is general allegation of pressing of neck upon the victim but same is not supported by any other witness and hence, framing of charge under Section 307 of I.P.C is illegal.

It is submitted that learned Court below has failed to consider that a simple case of 498-A of IPC has been converted into a case of serious nature like 307 IPC though there is no evidence either in the case diary or in the FIR.
It is further submitted that learned Court below ought to have considered that the entire occurrence had taken place at Patna.

5. It is further submitted that even one Mishal Kumar Arya, who is the second son in-law of the petitioner no.2, is disturbing the environment amongst both the petitioners on one hand and O.P.

It is submitted that the O.P. No.2 does not want to live with the petitioner no.1.

Even said Mishal Kumar Arya had disturbed the married life of Sakchi Kumari Verma who is sister of petitioner no.1 and daughter of petitioner no.2 and for which she has filed one Complaint Case No.269/03/17 dated 27.06.2017 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Tis Hazari Court, Delhi.

and hence the impugned order may be set aside.

disposed of on 24.10.2013 and 2020 (0) AIJEL- SC 66560 (Kaushik Chatterjee vs. State of Haryana)

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned APP for the State has submitted that the impugned order passed by the learned Court below is fit and proper and no interference is required.

It is submitted that the petitioners had threatened and assaulted the informant for demand of dowry and even blood had started oozing out from her mouth and nose and thus the offence under Section 307 of IPC is made out against both the petitioners.
It is submitted that prosecution witnesses have fully supported the case of the informant and hence this Criminal Revision Application may be dismissed.
7. Learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 after adopting the submissions of learned APP, has submitted that this Criminal Revision Application is devoid of merit.

It is submitted that this Criminal Revision Application has also become infructuous as the case has been fixed at the stage of evidence and four (04) witnesses have been examined so far and the photo copy of the statement of witnesses have been annexed as Annexure-A series.
It is submitted that both the petitioners, particularly petitioner no.1 had assaulted the informant-O.P. No.2 mercilessly.

It is submitted that the child of the O.P.
No.2 had been taken away by the petitioners against her wishes.
It is submitted that even on 03.04.2017 the informant-O.P.No.2 had lodged complaint before Mahila Helpline, Patna regarding the assault committed upon her by her husband and other in-law members.
8. It is submitted that even petitioner no.1 tried to kill O.P. No.2.
However, she could manage to save her life by fleeing away and therefore, sufficient evidence has already been collected during investigation to constitute the offence under Section 307 of IPC.
It is submitted that there is sufficient evidence available on record against both the petitioners to frame charges under Section 307 of IPC and allied sections of IPC.

It is submitted that for constituting an offence under Section 307 of the IPC, the intention of the accused to commit murder is required to be seen and there is no requirement of injury report or even necessity for a person to suffer any serious bodily injury for the purpose of maintaining a charge under Section 307 IPC.
In the instant case, the O.P. no.2 saved her life by fleeing away in an injured condition to the Women's Helpline from where she was rescued by her parents.

It is submitted that the accused persons have tortured the O.P. No.2 and have ill-treated her, assaulted her for dowry and have also attempted to take away her life and, therefore,
there are sufficient evidences, for which police, after investigation has submitted charge sheet against both the petitioners.

It is submitted that both Patna Court/Jamshedpur Court have Aditya Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173037545/
3 concurrent jurisdiction and accordingly the case was instituted at Jamshedpur.

sentences.text: It is submitted that an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by petitioner no.1 only to save his skin from criminal prosecution and in order to build a defence.

It is submitted that petitioner no.1 has already solemnized his second marriage during subsistence of his first marriage with O.P.
No.2 and they in order to put pressure upon the O.P. No.2 by deceitful means, had taken the custody of her minor daughter and have not allowed O.P. No.2 to meet her daughter since last five years.
9. It is further submitted that police have recorded the statement of several witnesses during investigation and they had supported the case of informant-O.P. No.2.

It is further submitted that even P.W-1 to P.W-4 namely Arun Gupta, Indrani Gupta, Mishal Arya and Shrija Verma have fully supported the case and P.W-4 is the informant herself and thus, this Criminal Revision Application has become infructuous and hence this Criminal Revision Application may be dismissed.

10. Perused the records of this case and considered the submission of both the sides.
11.

It transpires that both the petitioners of this Criminal Revision Application are the husband and mother in-law of the informant and informant has lodged the FIR against her husband, father in-law, mother in-law and Nanad on 01.10.2017 for demanding dowry and for assaulting her and for giving birth to a girl child and which has been kept by her in-law members while they were attending counseling at Patna.

12. It reveals from the FIR that marriage was solemnized between the petitioner no.1 and the O.P.
No.2 on 22.11.2010 but the first dispute between the parties arose on the birth of her daughter for which she was tortured and administered medicines of mental illness but neither the name of medicine nor the name of any doctor, from whom she was treated, has been stated.
However no complaint was made by the informant or her any other family members.

13. Thereafter, it transpires that main dispute arose for the first time in March, 2017 when she was allegedly mercilessly assaulted by her husband and who had allegedly tried to kill her by pressing her neck which is said to have resulted into oozing out blood from her mouth and nose and for which she anyhow saved her life by coming to Mahila Helpline and has also enclosed the copy of Mahila Helpline submitted on 08.03.2017 with the FIR marked as Annexure-2.
14.

From perusal of Mahila Helpline complaint dated 08.03.2017 before Mahila Helpline, Patna, it would appear that she has stated to the effect that her husband had mercilessly assaulted her yesterday night i.e. on 07.03.2017 and they had assaulted her earlier also and wanted to make her mad and they used to abuse her and had snatched her mobile phone yesterday and she was threatened by her mother in-law by mobile phone.

Therefore, the allegation of blood oozing out from her mouth and nose have also not been mentioned in the complaint made before the Mahila Helpline enclosed as Annexure-2 of this Criminal Revision Application, although it has been alleged in the FIR instituted on 01.10.2017.

Even it would appear that after March, counseling between the parties started and her husband (i.e. petitioner no.1) had visited the house of her father on 09.06.2017 at Jamshedpur and abused her and her father and went away by taking her daughter.

sentences.text: Thus, it is evident that the FIR was lodged on 01.10.2017 although last occurrence allegedly had taken place at Jamshedpdur when only petitioner no.1 had arrived at Jamshedpur and abused the informant namely Shrija Verma and her father.
She has also alleged that her husband is threatening her still on phone and abusing her father.

Thus, there is delay of around four months in lodging the FIR of the occurrence taking place on 09.06.2017 on which date the petitioner no.1 had allegedly abused and threatened the informant and had taken away the daughter of the informant.
However, the police has not instituted any case of abduction of daughter of the informant.

16. It further appears from the scanned copy of the Lower Court Records that the police has submitted charge sheet on 07.12.2018 under Sections 341/323/307/498-A of the IPC against both the petitioners only and observed that there is lack of evidence against the father in-law-Sanjay Verma and Nanad- Sakchi Verma.

Thus, even at the time of submission of the charge sheet, the police had not found the case of abduction of child of the informant by the petitioner no.1.
17.

The judgment reported in 2020 (0) AIJEL-SC 66560 (Kaushik Chatterjee vs. State of Haryana) is concerned, the same is not applicable in the case of the petitioners as it relates to decide the jurisdiction of the trial which was challenged and the Supreme Court had held that plea of lack of jurisdiction is to be decided by the trial court by leading evidence on the question of fact that may fall within the purview of Section 177 to 184 read with Section 26 of the Cr.P.C and invite a finding and the Hon'ble Supreme Court has rejected the plea of transfer of case.

sentences.text: 19 . It further transpires that the learned Court below had framed the charges against both the petitioners on 16.08.2019 for the offences under Sections 498A/34 and 307/34 of the IPC to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

Lower Court Records were not received by this Court till 13.12.2022, however, in the meantime,
further proceeding of the court below was stayed by the order passed by this Court on 14.09.2022 when the case was admitted and Lower Court Records were called for.
20.

Later on when the case was placed on 13.01.2023 the office has pointed out that Lower Court Records were not received but later on the office rectified its mistake and pointed out that Lower Court Records were received and till that date counter affidavit was not filed on behalf of the O.P.
No.2.

sentences.text: A counter affidavit has also been filed on behalf of the informant-O.P. No.2 on 18.01.2023 in which she has enclosed the deposition of evidence of witnesses namely namely, Arun Gupta, Indrani Gupta, Mishal Arya (brother in-law of petitioner no.1) and Shrija Verma (i.e. the informant) who have been examined as P.W-1 to P.W-4 respectively.

However, P.W-1- Shrija Verma has been examined fully but cross-examined in part till 21.07.2022.
22.

Therefore, it would appear that petitioners on the one hand are contesting the case before the learned Court below and on the other hand they have been arguing this Criminal Revision Application without making any amendment in the Criminal Revision Application and they have not challenged even the order framing charges passed by the learned Court below on 16.08.2019.
23.

Although this Criminal Revision Application has been filed on 25.11.2019 but the petitioners were not aware of the factual position and even they had filed supplementary affidavit on 22.08.2022 by giving various statements and bringing certain documents on record including the order of anticipatory bail and order sheet of M.T.S. No.670 of 2017 and other documents still they have not challenged the order framing charges.

24. O.P. No.2 has filed supplementary counter affidavit also on 27.04.2023 and enclosed the prescription dated 15.03.2017 which also reveals that O.P. No.2 had blood clot on right eye and swelling on head on right side which was issued by the private doctor namely Dr. K.S.P Gupta,
Jamshedpur and not even by the Government doctor.
However, the said document was not handed over to the police during investigation.

25. It further transpires that although the learned Court below has sent the Lower Court Records and from perusal of the case diary it would appear that police has submitted charge sheet under Section 307/323/498-A/34 of the IPC without any injury report and thus offence under Section 307 IPC is not made out.
26.

Although, this Court finds that prima facie, no case under Section 307 IPC is made out rather this Court finds from the plain reading of the FIR and the charge sheet that at best it can be a case under Section 323 and 498-A but trial under Section 307 IPC is not permissible.

27. It appears that there is manifest error on the part of the learned Court below while framing charges under Section 307 IPC against the petitioners in absence of injury report and in absence of gross delay in lodging the FIR and on the distorted fact of abduction of daughter of the informant.
28. It is well settled that if the foundation is wrong then the Court can set aside the proceeding at any stage irrespective of the fact that the prosecution witnesses have been examined.

29. It has been held by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 03.03.2023 passed in W.P. (Cr.) no.483 of 2022 (Rajesh Kacchap and Ors. vs. State of Jharkhand and Ors.) at paragraph nos.37 and 38 as follows:-

Mr. Ranjit Kumar, the learned senior counsel for the petitioners has referred to "Ritesh Tewari"19, "Davinder Pal Singh Bhullar"20 and "Kavita Manikikar"21, to put forth a proposition that once registration of zero FIR on 31st July 2022 by the officer- in-charge of Argora PS at Ranchi and transfer of zero FIR to Panchla PS on the same day are held illegal the consequences shall follow as expressed in Latin maxim"sublato fundamento cadit opus", which means when foundation is removed the superstructure falls. The law as has been laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforementioned cases is very clear that every subsequent acts/actions taken pursuant to any order or decision, or act or omission on the part of the authority shall be non est."

However, this Court refrains itself from setting aside the entire impugned order as the petitioners have not amended the prayer till date and have not challenged the order framing charges and have failed to make necessary amendment even after receiving counter affidavit and supplementary counter affidavit filed on behalf of the informant-O.P. No.2.
34.

Accordingly, the order dated 02.08.2019 passed by the learned Court below is set aside in part to the extent that charges can be framed under Sections 341, 323, 498A/34 of the IPC except Section 307 of IPC and the matter is remitted to the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class/Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur having jurisdiction of Jugsalai P.S. Case No.92 of 2017, arising out of G.R. Case No.2718/2017 and the trial shall proceed further in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class/Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is submitted that for constituting an offence under Section 307 of the IPC, the intention of the accused to commit murder is required to be seen and there is no requirement of injury report or even necessity for a person to suffer any serious bodily injury for the purpose of maintaining a charge under Section 307 IPC.
It is submitted that both Patna Court/Jamshedpur Court have Aditya Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173037545/
3 concurrent jurisdiction and accordingly the case was instituted at Jamshedpur.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even it would appear that after March, counseling between the parties started and her husband (i.e. petitioner no.1) had visited the house of her father on 09.06.2017 at Jamshedpur and abused her and her father and went away by taking her daughter.
Aditya Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173037545/
4 15.
Thus, it is evident that the FIR was lodged on 01.10.2017 although last occurrence allegedly had taken place at Jamshedpdur when only petitioner no.1 had arrived at Jamshedpur and abused the informant namely Shrija Verma and her father.
She has also alleged that her husband is threatening her still on phone and abusing her father.
Thus, there is delay of around four months in lodging the FIR of the occurrence taking place on 09.06.2017 on which date the petitioner no.1 had allegedly abused and threatened the informant and had taken away the daughter of the informant.
However, the police has not instituted any case of abduction of daughter of the informant.
Thus, even at the time of submission of the charge sheet, the police had not found the case of abduction of child of the informant by the petitioner no.1.
17.
The judgment reported in 2020 (0) AIJEL-SC 66560 (Kaushik Chatterjee vs. State of Haryana) is concerned, the same is not applicable in the case of the petitioners as it relates to decide the jurisdiction of the trial which was challenged and the Supreme Court had held that plea of lack of jurisdiction is to be decided by the trial court by leading evidence on the question of fact that may fall within the purview of Section 177 to 184 read with Section 26 of the Cr.P.C and invite a finding and the Hon'ble Supreme Court has rejected the plea of transfer of case.
18. The judgment reported in 2013 (0) AIJEL-SC 54599 (Krishna Reddy vs. State By Station House Officer) is not applicable in the present case as the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this case has held that charge sheet does not indicate any complicity for the parents of the deceased as they were living separately and there was no case of demand of dowry by the in- laws of the deceased and Hon'ble Supreme Court had upheld the discharge of the parents of the deceased.
Aditya Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173037545/
5 21.
Although this Criminal Revision Application has been filed on 25.11.2019 but the petitioners were not aware of the factual position and even they had filed supplementary affidavit on 22.08.2022 by giving various statements and bringing certain documents on record including the order of anticipatory bail and order sheet of M.T.S. No.670 of 2017 and other documents still they have not challenged the order framing charges.
Although, this Court finds that prima facie, no case under Section 307 IPC is made out rather this Court finds from the plain reading of the FIR and the charge sheet that at best it can be a case under Section 323 and 498-A but trial under Section 307 IPC is not permissible.
27. It appears that there is manifest error on the part of the learned Court below while framing charges under Section 307 IPC against the petitioners in absence of injury report and in absence of gross delay in lodging the FIR and on the distorted fact of abduction of daughter of the informant.
28. It is well settled that if the foundation is wrong then the Court can set aside the proceeding at any stage irrespective of the fact that the prosecution witnesses have been examined.
(Vide Upen Chandra Gogoi v. State of Assam [(1998) 3 SCC 381 : 1998 SCC (L&S) 872] ; Satchidananda Misra v. State of Orissa [(2004) 8 SCC 599 : 2004 SCC (L&S) 1181] and SBI v. Rakesh Kumar Tewari [(2006) 1 SCC 530 : 2006 SCC (L&S) 143] .)
Para-34:- In Mangal Prasad Tamoli v.
Narvadeshwar Mishra [(2005) 3 SCC 422
In such a fact situation, the legal maxim sublato fundamento cadit opusmeaning thereby that foundation being removed, structure/work falls, comes into play and applies on all scores in the present case.
